items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 9:1
items.html: (To the question) What are wide paths? The vessels of the HGT of ZA, in which the Yesod of Ima, called Or [path], is clothed, are discerned as receiving the influx in wide paths. For the Yesod of Ima shines the light of Hassadim in width, as is known, and therefore the Yesod of Ima is called short and wide. However, after the Yesod of Ima is cut off, namely from the point of the chest and below, which are the vessels of the NHY, the influx of the Hassadim of the Yesod of Ima that come in width is cut off from there, and therefore the NHY are called narrow vessels, since all their correction is in the Yesod of Aba, which is an aspect of narrow and long, and therefore they are discerned as receiving the influx from the aspect of narrow paths, for the Yesod of Aba is called a path. (Item 96).
